issues.legal_issue: Summary eviction proceedings cannot be used to remove an occupant who raises a bona fide claim to remain in possession that requires adjudication of complex questions of law or fact.
material_facts: The authorities initiated summary proceedings to evict the respondent from land recorded as government land.
The respondent claimed a right to remain in possession based on an earlier government grant, tenancy rules and enactments, revenue records, and other documents.
Determining the respondent’s claim required interpreting laws and documents and investigating disputed facts through evidence.
issues.conclusion: The summary proceedings were invalid, and the orders made in those proceedings were set aside. The Court did not determine the parties’ rights to the land, leaving the State free to pursue an appropriate remedy before a competent forum.
issues.legal_principle: Section 91 of the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956 provides a summary procedure for evicting a person in unauthorised occupation of government land, but that procedure is unsuitable for adjudicating a bona fide claim to possession involving complicated questions of title. Relying on the analogous rule under Section 6 of the Andhra Pradesh Land Encroachment Act, 1945, stated in Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Thummala Krishna Rao, 1982 (3) SCR 5000, the Court held that such a claim must be resolved through ordinary proceedings before an appropriate forum.

predicates.summary_eviction_proceeding: Authorities initiated a summary proceeding to remove a person alleged to occupy government land without authority.
predicates.occupant_raises_bona_fide_possession_cla: The occupant asserted a bona fide legal basis for remaining in possession of the land.
predicates.claim_requires_complex_adjudication: Resolving the occupant’s claim required adjudicating complex questions of law or fact, including investigation of disputed facts.

issues.definition: When authorities use a summary eviction proceeding against an occupant who raises a bona fide possession claim requiring complex adjudication, the proceeding cannot determine that claim.
